claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for launch is policy-compliant and evidentially supported despite a known model-card weakness in the grant compliance review segment that remains exposed in the initial rollout.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the stated policy threshold.
If the affected use case remains exposed, rollout controls and monitoring are not enough by themselves.
A reviewed risk acceptance or exclusion of the affected use case is the key missing predicate.
Public best-practice guidance can support context, but it cannot substitute for required case-specific approval or disclosure evidence.
evidence_requests: Reviewed risk acceptance explicitly covering the grant compliance review exposure.
Evidence that the affected use case is excluded from the initial rollout cohort, if that is the intended mitigation.
The actual model-card or disclosure record showing the known limitation is documented, reviewed, and tied to launch approval.
Approval documentation showing the certifier accepted launch with this specific exposed weakness under policy.
specific_concerns: The actor summary itself states the affected grant compliance review segment remains in scope for the initial rollout.
The available risk acceptance is described as a draft, incomplete, and not addressing the exposed segment.
The governing policy requires either exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance; the summary provides neither.
Rollout controls cited by the actor (6% rollout, rollback, monitoring) do not satisfy the stated policy when the affected segment remains exposed.
The packet relies on public guidance about monitoring and documentation, but that does not establish that the required model-card disclosure or approval actually exists in this case.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the present record.
That launch-time disclosure is part of the certification posture; no admissible evidence of an actual reviewed disclosure artifact is identified.
That overall readiness and reversible deployment are sufficient to overcome the unresolved policy predicate for the exposed weak segment.
